The Coprates Rim Hotel, Valles Marineris, Mars

Some centuries from now, a tourist on Mars. You stand in a hotel's glass observation lounge on the north rim of Coprates Chasma (11.75° S, 62.70° W), where Valles Marineris, the canyon as long as the United States is wide, is 10 km deep. A glass-floored deck runs out over the drop. Gravity is 0.38 g; outside, the air is 0.6% of Earth's, so through the airlock you wear a suit. The sky is butterscotch, blue round the setting Sun; Phobos crosses it west to east twice a sol.

The ground is real: Mars as NASA's laser altimeter measured it, 463 m between points here and 1.85 km across the rest of Valles Marineris; smaller detail is generated. The colony is imagined, built the way physics says it would have to be: people live under rock and regolith.

The hotel works the way a real one would have to: everything a guest uses is joined by pressurised corridors buried under regolith, so you go about in ordinary clothes. Follow the green arrows from the lounge to the hub (lobby, café, a small park), and from there to the Canyon Lift (down the wall to the canyon floor, 10 km below), the maglev (570 km to the Melas Overlook), the rover garage, the greenhouse, the tram to the rocket port, and the suit room. To walk outside, use a suitport. Walk up to anything and press E (A in VR). Rides are sped up.

WASD walk  ·  drag to look  ·  shift run  ·  space jump  ·  E ride, drive, get out, or info on what you look at  ·  in the rover WS drive, AD steer  ·  T speed up time  ·  L labels  ·  H readout  ·  M sitting / standing  ·  R back to the lounge
In VR: left stick walk or drive (left trigger runs), right stick turn, B jump, A or right trigger: ride, drive, get out, or info, Y speed up time, X labels, click the left stick: sitting / standing; the readout is on your left wrist

Elevations: Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA), Mars Global Surveyor, NASA PDS. Loading the ground…
